issue.title: Add Global Disable switch / kill switch / maintenance mode

labels.name: needs-triage
labels.description: label for new issues that we didn't triage yet

repository.name: airflow
repository.description: Apache Airflow - A platform to programmatically author, schedule, and monitor workflows

issue.body:
### Description

Currently Dags can be enabled or disabled on a per-dag level, but the airflow deployment itself cannot be disabled. This means that if a new airflow deployment is brought up, and dags are automatically enabled (e.g. by setting `is_paused_upon_creation=False`) then they will start automatically running as soon as they are parsed and the instance is deployed.

### Use case/motivation

Add a global toggle switch that can be managed by Deployment managers / (Super) Admins that disables all scheduling of dags when toggled.
This could be used to put airflow into a 'maintenance mode' where no tasks will be scheduled, but running tasks can be drained, and the UI is still accessible. This allows deployment managers to perform maintenance work such as database upgrades, airflow upgrades etc. with confidence that nothing will be scheduled until the toggle is re-enabled.

### Related issues

#70172

### Are you willing to submit a PR?

- [ ] Yes I am willing to submit a PR!

### Code of Conduct

- [x] I agree to follow this project's [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/apache/airflow/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)

body: This is partially enabled in the UI in 3.4.0 with filtering dags by not paused dags and then pausing all or draining all at once. It has some pagination limits, but it will be a lot less bad than before.

Thanks @bbovenzi , I think the existing bulk pause/drain functionality addresses a related use case, but not quite the one proposed here.

The key requirement is that a global pause must not modify the individual DAGs' is_paused state.

For example, if A and B are active and C is intentionally paused, a global pause should leave the stored state as:

```
A: is_paused = false
B: is_paused = false
C: is_paused = true
```

The scheduler would simply treat all three as paused while the global override is enabled. Disabling the override would then immediately restore the previous behavior without needing to track or restore any DAG state.

With the current bulk pause approach, A and B would be changed to is_paused = true, and bulk unpausing them later could also unpause C unless the previous state is tracked separately.

So I see the 3.4 UI functionality as helpful for bulk operations, but the proposal here is specifically for a scheduler level override, rather than a bulk mutation of per DAG pause state.

issue.title: Pause a Dag for a set time and resume it automatically

repository.name: airflow
repository.description: Apache Airflow - A platform to programmatically author, schedule, and monitor workflows

issue.body:
### Description

Let users pause a Dag for a set time, such as 1 hour, 4 hours, or until a chosen date and time. When the time is up, Airflow unpauses the Dag on its own.

In the UI, the pause toggle could offer a few choices: pause until I turn it back on (today's behavior), pause for 1 hour, pause for 4 hours, pause for 1 day, or pause until a date and time. While a timed pause is active, the Dag list and the Dag page would show when the Dag comes back on. The same option would help in the REST API and the CLI.

I'm happy to build this and open a PR. Before I start, I'd welcome a steer on whether this fits Airflow and how you'd like it shaped.

### Use case/motivation

We often need to stop a Dag for a short, known period: database maintenance, a vendor outage, or a holiday. As of Airflow 3.3.2, a pause has no end time, so someone has to remember to unpause the Dag. When they forget, the Dag stays off and data quietly goes stale. Others looking at the UI also can't tell whether a paused Dag is meant to stay off or should already be back on.

The workarounds live outside the pause button: a cron job, or a separate Dag that unpauses through the CLI or the API. People forget they exist, and nothing in the UI shows that a resume is planned.

What I'd like to happen:

- When I pause a Dag, I can choose how long it stays paused, or until when.
- At that time, Airflow unpauses the Dag, just as if someone had clicked the toggle.
- The UI shows that the Dag is paused until a given time.
- I can still unpause early or change the end time.

### Related issues

- #15675 asks for an optional reason when pausing a Dag. A comment there also asks for an unpause time, but the issue itself is about the reason.
- #16349 asked for this same timed unpause in 2021. It was closed as a duplicate of #15675.
- #69699 proposes a global pause for maintenance. It freezes the whole deployment and has no end time, so it solves a different problem.

### Are you willing to submit a PR?

- [x] Yes I am willing to submit a PR!

### Code of Conduct

- [x] I agree to follow this project's Code of Conduct
